 Judgment
1. MFA Nos.4150/2021 and 4187/2021 under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')

have been filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the judgment dated 20.04.2021 passed by MACT, Bengaluru in MVC Nos.6229/2018 and 6230/2018,
respectively.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals briefly stated are that 05.09.2018 at about 3.00 a.m.,
the claimant-Ashok M N in MVC No.6229/2018 and Prajwal Kumar H in MVC No.6230/2018 along with others was traveling in Omni Car bearing Registration No.KA-02-MN- NC: 2023:KHC:45303 4750 on NH-4, Tumkur-Sira Road, near Kataveeranahalli Gate, Kallambella Hobli, Sira Taluk, Tumkur District, at the same time, both drivers of the Car and the driver of the Lorry bearing Registration No.KA-02-AD-9547 were being driven rashly and recklessly and negligently with high speed endangering human life and property and without given any signal and parked the right side of the Highway Road and dashed the Lorry.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, both claimants sustained grievous injuries and were hospitalized.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that they spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges, etc.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred purely on account of the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicles by its drivers.
4. On service of notice, the respondent Nos.2 and 4 appeared through counsel and filed written statement in NC: 2023:KHC:45303 which the averments made in the petition were denied.
It was pleaded that the petitions themselves are false and frivolous in the eye of law.
The age, avocation and income of the claimants and the medical expenses are denied.
It was further pleaded that the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant.
Hence, they sought for dismissal of the petition.

The respondent Nos.1 and 3 did not appear before the Tribunal inspite of service of notice and were placed ex-parte.

sentences.text: On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.

The claimant in MVC No.6229/2018 himself was examined as PW-1 and the claimant in MVC No.6230/2018 himself was examined as PW-2 and Dr.Nagaraj B N was examined as PW-10 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P67.
On behalf of the respondents, two witnesses were examined as RW-1 and NC: 2023:KHC:45303 RW-2 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its drivers,
as a result of which, the claimants sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant in MVC No.6229/2018 is entitled to a compensation of Rs.7,04,000/- and claimant in MVC No.6230/2018 is entitled to a compensation of Rs.5,18,000/- along with interest at the rate of 9%
p.a. and directed both Insurance Companies to deposit the compensation amount along with interest excluding the interest for future medical expenses.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.

The learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
NC: 2023:KHC:45303 a) Firstly, even though the claimant claims that he was working as coolie and agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken the notional income as merely as Rs.10,500/- p.m.
b) Secondly, the claimant has examined the doctor as PW-10.
The doctor in his evidence has stated that the claimant has suffered physical disability of 38% to lower limb and 26% to whole body.
But the Tribunal has taken the whole body disability at 18%, which is on the lower side.
c) Thirdly, due to the accident, the claimant has sustained grievous injuries.
He was treated as inpatient for a period of 10 days.
Even after discharge from the hospital, he was not in a position to discharge his regular work.
He has suffered lot of pain during treatment.

Considering the same, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the heads of 'loss of amenities', 'pain and sufferings', 'future medical expenses' and other incidental expenses are on the lower side.
Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for ICICI Lambard and Royal Sundaram General Insurance Companies has raised the following counter-contentions:

ORDER a) The appeals are allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
c) The claimant in MFA No.4150/2021 (MVC No.6229/2018) is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.8,16,000/-.
d) The claimant MFA No.4187/2021 (MVC No.6230/2018) is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.7,61,000/-.

In view of judgment of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of 'MS.JOYEETA BOSE'
(supra), the enhanced compensation shall carry interest at 6% per annum.

f) Both ICICI Lambard and Royal Sundaram General Insurance Companies are directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest in the ratio of 50:50 from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment excluding interest for the compensation awarded under the head of 'future medical expenses'.
